newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan PM asks Peru president for caution in siege.
newsitem.headline: Japan PM asks Peru president for caution in siege.

text.p: Japan's prime minister told the president of Peru on Tuesday he was concerned about police manoeuvres that have drawn gunfire from guerrillas holding 72 people hostage in the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima.

"We understand the need to tighten security at the compound but ask that you give sufficient consideration to preventing accidents or incidents," government spokesman Seiroku Kajiyama quoted Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto as telling President Alberto Fujimori by phone.
The spokesman declined to reveal the response of Fujimori, who he said called Hashimoto and explained Lima's stance on the six-week-old standoff.
Hashimoto earlier expressed for the second day in a row concern about Peruvian police moves.
"I'm worried if the terrorists have been irritated over moves of the (Peruvian) special forces. We are asking for care to be taken about such moves," Hashimoto told reporters.

Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) guerrillas fired several shots on Monday at armoured vehicles of Peru's crack anti-terrorist squad who were parading around the residence and blaring military music through loudspeakers.
One of the vehicles was hit, but there were no immediate reports of any injuries.
On Monday, Hashimoto asked Peru to limit police manoeuvres around the diplomatic residence, fearing they could unsettle the hostages held by the MRTA.
